description.narrative: The Project consists of the development, financing, construction, operation, and maintenance of the greenfield Mmadinare 50MWac Solar PV Facility (the Project) in a 140 hectares site located approximately 5.8km northwest of Selebi Phikwe and 9.2km southeast from Mmadinare, in the Selebi Phikwe District of Botswana. The Mmadinare Project (Phase II) is a replica and adjacent to the 50 MWac Selebi Phikwe Project (Phase I) that is currently under construction bringing the total capacity of the Mmadinare Solar complex to 100 MWac.

The main expected project-level outcomes stem from increased access to reliable electricity through investment in renewable energy. Botswana is currently facing energy insecurity and loadshedding due to a demand deficit and dependency on imports from South Africa. The project is expected to increase the installed generation capacity of Botswana at an affordable tariff. The proposed investment will also contribute to reducing GHG emissions from electricity generation given the heavy reliance of Botswana's power generation on coal fired power stations, diesel peakers and imports from South Africa, which is still mostly coal based The anticipated market creation effects include improved competitiveness, deriving from support to the country's second utility scale project-financed IPP project, following up on IFC support for the first such IPP, with important demonstration effects and a signal to investors of the bankability of similar projects within a evolving regulatory context. This investment also supports Botswana's efforts to increase resilience, by demonstrating a commercially viable and sustainable way to diversify the countrys energy mix and transition out of its current expensive and unreliable dependence on fossil fuel-based energy and imports from South Africa.

name.narrative: The Project is located close to Selebi Phikwe town and will interconnect to the newly built 33/220kV Mmadinare Substation that feeds into the transmission line between Selebi Phikwe and Phokoje substation. The Phokoje substation is situated on the Southern African Power Pool (SAPP) north-south 400kV transmission backbone providing the Project a stable point of interconnection as well as a strategic location in respect of the SAPP. The Project will cover an area of approximately 140ha and will have an installed peak capacity of 60MWp, making use of single axis trackers and bifacial solar panels.
